definitions.title: Gradient Vector
definitions.latex: \nabla f(x, y) = f_x \mathbf{i} + f_y \mathbf{j} = \langle f_x, f_y \rangle, \quad \nabla f(x, y, z) = \langle f_x, f_y, f_z \rangle
definitions.statement: The gradient of a differentiable scalar function f is the vector field whose components are the first partial derivatives of f.
definitions.explanation: Points in the direction of maximum instantaneous rate of increase of f, with magnitude |grad f| equal to that maximal rate.
definitions.keyTakeaway: grad f is everywhere orthogonal to the level curves or level surfaces of f.

definitions.title: Directional Derivative
definitions.latex: D_\mathbf{u} f(x_0, y_0) = \nabla f(x_0, y_0) \cdot \mathbf{u} = |\nabla f| \cos\theta
definitions.statement: The directional derivative of f in the direction of unit vector u is the scalar product of the gradient vector with u. It measures the rate of change of f moving through (x_0, y_0) along direction u.
definitions.explanation: Attains maximum value |grad f| when u is parallel to grad f (theta = 0); minimum -|grad f| when antiparallel (theta = pi); and zero when tangent to level curve (theta = pi/2).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Computes rate of change in any arbitrary spatial direction.
